column1: Anna Keay reviews Charles Spencer’s book about the hunt for King Charles II during the English Civil War of the seventeenth century
column2: 安娜·基评查尔斯·斯宾塞的著作，书中讲述了17世纪英国内战期间追捕国王查理二世的故事。
column5: King Charles II|国王查理二世

column1: Charles Spencer’s latest book, To Catch a King, tells us the story of the hunt for King Charles II in the six weeks after his resounding defeat at the Battle of Worcester in September 1651.
column2: 查尔斯·斯宾塞的新书《追捕国王》，讲述了1651年9月查理二世在伍斯特战役中惨败后，遭到追捕的那六周。

column1: And what a story it is.
column2: 这是个多么精彩的故事啊。
column3: what a story|多么精彩的故事（感叹）

column1: After his father was executed by the Parliamentarians in 1649, the young Charles II sacrificed one of the very principles his father had died for and did a deal with the Scots, thereby accepting Presbyterianism* as the national religion in return for being crowned King of Scots.
column2: 1649年，父亲被议会派处决后，年轻的查理二世放弃了父亲为之殉身的一项原则，与苏格兰人达成协议，接受长老宗*为国教，以换取加冕为苏格兰国王。
column7: did a deal with|与……达成协议

column1: His arrival in Edinburgh prompted the English Parliamentary army to invade Scotland in a pre-emptive strike.
column2: 他抵达爱丁堡，促使英格兰议会军先发制人，入侵苏格兰。

column1: This was followed by a Scottish invasion of England.
column2: 接着，苏格兰军队入侵英格兰。

column1: The two sides finally faced one another at Worcester in the west of England in 1651.
column2: 1651年，双方终于在英格兰西部的伍斯特正面交锋。
column5: faced one another|与对方正面交锋

column1: After being comprehensively defeated on the meadows outside the city by the Parliamentarian army, the 21-year-old king found himself the subject of a national manhunt, with a huge sum offered for his capture.
column2: 在城外的草地上被议会军彻底击败后，年仅21岁的国王随即成了全国搜捕的对象，擒获他的人可得一大笔赏金。

column1: Over the following six weeks he managed, through a series of heart-poundingly close escapes, to evade the Parliamentarians before seeking refuge in France.
column2: 在接下来的六周里，他几次惊险脱身，终于逃过议会派的追捕，随后到法国寻求庇护。

column1: For the next nine years, the penniless and defeated Charles wandered around Europe with only a small group of loyal supporters.
column2: 此后的九年里，战败且身无分文的查理在欧洲各地辗转，身边只有一小群忠实的支持者。

column1: Years later, after his restoration as king, the 50-year-old Charles II requested a meeting with the writer and diarist Samuel Pepys.
column2: 多年以后，已恢复王位的查理二世年届五十，提出要与作家兼日记作者塞缪尔·佩皮斯会面。

column1: His intention when asking Pepys to commit his story to paper was to ensure that this most extraordinary episode was never forgotten.
column2: 他请佩皮斯把自己的故事记录下来，是希望这段非同寻常的经历永远不被遗忘。
column4: commit his story to paper|把……记录下来

column1: Over two three-hour sittings, the king related to him in great detail his personal recollections of the six weeks he had spent as a fugitive.
column2: 国王分两次、每次三小时，向他详细讲述了自己对那六周逃亡生活的回忆。

column1: As the king and secretary settled down (a scene that is surely a gift for a future scriptwriter), Charles commenced his story: ‘After the battle was so absolutely lost as to be beyond hope of recovery, I began to think of the best way of saving myself.’
column2: 国王和书记员坐定后（这场面一定会让日后写剧本的人求之不得），查理开始讲述：“那一仗败得彻底，已经毫无挽回的希望，我就开始琢磨怎样才能最好地自保。”
column8: beyond hope of recovery|毫无挽回的希望

column1: One of the joys of Spencer’s book, a result not least of its use of Charles II’s own narrative as well as those of his supporters, is just how close the reader gets to the action.
column2: 阅读斯宾塞这本书的一大乐趣，是读者仿佛置身事发现场。这很大程度上要归功于作者既引用了支持者的记述，也引用了查理二世本人的回忆。
column4: not least|尤其；在很大程度上

column1: The day-by-day retelling of the fugitives’ doings provides delicious details: the cutting of the king’s long hair with agricultural shears, the use of walnut leaves to dye his pale skin, and the day Charles spent lying on a branch of the great oak tree in Boscobel Wood as the Parliamentary soldiers scoured the forest floor below.
column2: 书中逐日复述了逃亡者的行踪，写下许多引人入胜的细节：有人用农用剪刀剪去国王的长发，用胡桃叶给他苍白的皮肤染色。有一天，查理整日躺在博斯科贝尔林中一棵大橡树的枝头，而议会军士兵正在树下的林地上仔细搜索。

column1: Spencer draws out both the humour – such as the preposterous refusal of Charles’s friend Henry Wilmot to adopt disguise on the grounds that it was beneath his dignity – and the emotional tension when the secret of the king’s presence was cautiously revealed to his supporters.
column2: 斯宾塞既写出了幽默，比如查理的朋友亨利·威尔莫特荒唐地拒绝乔装，理由是这样有失身份；也写出了情绪上的紧张：人们小心翼翼地向支持者透露了国王就在场的秘密。
column8: on the grounds that|以……为理由

column1: Charles’s adventures after losing the Battle of Worcester hide the uncomfortable truth that whilst almost everyone in England had been appalled by the execution of his father, they had not welcomed the arrival of his son with the Scots army, but had instead firmly bolted their doors.
column2: 查理在伍斯特战败后的冒险故事掩盖了一个令人不安的事实：尽管英格兰几乎人人都对其父遭处决感到震惊，但人们并不欢迎儿子随苏格兰军队到来，反倒把家门闩得严严实实。

column1: This was partly because he rode at the head of what looked like a foreign invasion force and partly because, after almost a decade of civil war, people were desperate to avoid it beginning again.
column2: 原因一是查理骑马领头而来的部队看起来像是外国入侵之师；二是内战已持续近十年，人们唯恐战火重燃。
column4: at the head of|在……的前头

column1: This makes it all the more interesting that Charles II himself loved the story so much ever after.
column2: 正因如此，查理二世本人后来一直如此喜爱这个故事，就更耐人寻味了。

column1: As well as retelling it to anyone who would listen, causing eye-rolling among courtiers, he set in train a series of initiatives to memorialise it.
column2: 他逢人肯听就要重讲这个故事，讲得朝臣们直翻白眼；另外，他还推动了一系列纪念这段经历的举措。

column1: There was to be a new order of chivalry, the Knights of the Royal Oak.
column2: 按计划，还要设立一个新的骑士团，名为皇家橡树骑士团。
column3: There was to be|原计划要有
column5: Knights of the Royal Oak|皇家橡树骑士团

column1: A series of enormous oil paintings depicting the episode were produced, including a two-metre-wide canvas of Boscobel Wood and a set of six similarly enormous paintings of the king on the run.
column2: 人们还创作了一系列描绘这段经历的巨幅油画，包括一幅两米宽、以博斯科贝尔林为题材的画布油画，以及一组六幅同样巨大的国王出逃图。

column1: In 1660, Charles II commissioned the artist John Michael Wright to paint a flying squadron of cherubs* carrying an oak tree to the heavens on the ceiling of his bedchamber.
column2: 1660年，查理二世委托画家约翰·迈克尔·赖特，在寝宫的天花板上画了一队飞翔的小天使*，它们正抬着一棵橡树飞向天国。

column1: It is hard to imagine many other kings marking the lowest point in their life so enthusiastically, or indeed pulling off such an escape in the first place.
column2: 很难想象还有多少国王会如此热衷于纪念人生的最低谷，更难想象又有多少国王当初真能完成这样一次逃亡。

column1: Charles Spencer is the perfect person to pass the story on to a new generation.
column2: 把这个故事讲给新一代听，查尔斯·斯宾塞是再合适不过的人选。
column4: pass the story on|把故事传下去

column1: His pacey, readable prose steers deftly clear of modern idioms and elegantly brings to life the details of the great tale.
column2: 他的散文节奏明快、可读性强，巧妙避开了现代习语，又以优雅的笔触将这个精彩故事的细节写活了。

column1: He has even-handed sympathy for both the fugitive king and the fierce republican regime that hunted him, and he succeeds in his desire to explore far more of the background of the story than previous books on the subject have done.
column2: 对逃亡的国王与追捕他的严厉共和政权，他都抱有不偏不倚的同情。他本希望比此前探讨这一题材的书更深入地挖掘故事背景，也确实做到了。

column1: Indeed, the opening third of the book is about how Charles II found himself at Worcester in the first place, which for some will be reason alone to read To Catch a King.
column2: 的确，全书开头三分之一都在讲查理二世当初为何会出现在伍斯特；对有些人而言，仅此一点就值得读《追捕国王》。
column6: reason alone|单凭这一点就足够的理由

column1: The tantalising question left, in the end, is that of what it all meant.
column2: 最终留下的那个引人深思的问题是，这整段经历究竟意味着什么？

column1: Would Charles II have been a different king had these six weeks never happened?
column2: 如果这六周的经历从未发生，查理二世会成为一个不一样的国王吗？
column4: had these six weeks never happened|假如从未有过这六周（倒装假设）

column1: The days and nights spent in hiding must have affected him in some way.
column2: 那些东躲西藏的日日夜夜，一定以某种方式影响了他。

column1: Did the need to assume disguises, to survive on wit and charm alone, to use trickery and subterfuge to escape from tight corners help form him?
column2: 他不得不乔装打扮，仅凭机智和个人魅力度日，还要用计谋和欺瞒摆脱困境。这些经历是否帮助塑造了他的性格？

column1: This is the one area where the book doesn’t quite hit the mark.
column2: 这正是本书唯一没有写得十分到位的地方。

column1: Instead its depiction of Charles II in his final years as an ineffective, pleasure-loving monarch doesn’t do justice to the man (neither is it accurate), or to the complexity of his character.
column2: 书中只是把晚年的查理二世描绘成一个无能、贪图享乐的君主；这样的刻画既不准确，也没能公允地反映其人及其性格的复杂之处。
column8: do justice to|公允而充分地表现

column1: But this one niggle aside, To Catch a King is an excellent read, and those who come to it knowing little of the famous tale will find they have a treat in store.
column2: 除去这点小小的不满，《追捕国王》是一本极好的读物。那些原先对这个著名故事知之不多的读者，读来定会别有一番享受。
column5: an excellent read|一本极好的读物
column7: a treat in store|有一番乐趣在等着
